endowment_summary: Started baseball at age 10, showed exceptional physical talent with strong build and pitching ability. Underwent Tommy John surgery at 17 and recovered to win KBO Triple Crown, MVP, and Rookie of the Year at 19 — unprecedented in KBO history. Exceptional athletic prodigy with resilience.
inherited_summary: Father Jae-cheon was a passionate baseball fan who took sons to games from childhood, bought Hyun-jin a left-handed glove, and provided dedicated training including target practice and mental conditioning. Working-class family in Incheon; no wealth or industry connections.
ecosystem_summary: Korean baseball ecosystem with Dongsan High School's strong program and the KBO professional pipeline. Father's dedicated mentorship from childhood. Selected by Hanwha Eagles, providing direct entry to elite professional baseball at 19.

endowment_summary: Born during parents' circumnavigation, spent first five years at sea. Received first boat at 6, sailed solo from age 10, crossed English Channel solo at 13, completed solo circumnavigation at 16. Exceptional domain aptitude and drive from extremely young age.
inherited_summary: Father Dick Dekker is a self-taught boat engineer from a family of sailors. Mother Babs Müller was a circus artist. Born on parents' seven-year sailing voyage. Father provided direct sailing mentorship and built a houseboat they lived on. Parents divorced at 6; father raised her.
ecosystem_summary: Dutch sailing culture and father's dedicated mentorship from birth. Early and continuous access to boats — Optimist dinghy at 6, Hurley 700 at 11. Father supported her circumnavigation attempt despite Dutch government opposition and legal battles.

endowment_summary: Discovered StarCraft at 18 during third year of high school. Rapid rise to dominance by 21, winning OSL titles and WCG gold medals. Exceptional concentration and natural talent for gaming, but late discovery and no early cognitive prodigy indicators.
inherited_summary: Lacked money for his own computer, practically lived in PC bangs (internet cafes). Parents did not approve of gaming career. Working-class family in Seoul with no domain connections or resources for computing.
ecosystem_summary: South Korean PC bang culture and the birth of professional esports — he was at the epicenter of the esports revolution. Perfect timing: StarCraft launched in 1998, and Korea's pro gaming infrastructure emerged around him. Discovered by management company president at a PC bang in 1999.

endowment_summary: Started snooker at 10-11 at a club next to his home. Won national students championship in 2002. World Amateur champion at 23. Above-average natural talent but not a traditional prodigy; initially viewed snooker as a pastime while studying at technical college.
inherited_summary: Grew up near a small snooker club in Nakhon Nayok where his two elder brothers played. Working-class family; aspired to be an electrician. No family wealth, domain connections, or notable professional background.
ecosystem_summary: Snooker club next to family home provided early domain proximity. Elder brothers as peer competitors. Thai snooker pipeline influenced by James Wattana's earlier success. WPBSA Asian academy provided professional development. Regional ecosystem but not elite-level.

endowment_summary: Straight-A student ('vukovac') in primary school, trained handball for 8 years from age 12. Selected from over 6,000 applicants at BKTV at 19. Capable and disciplined but no prodigy-level indicators in media or entertainment.
inherited_summary: Father Jovan was a professor at the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, mother Jelena was in scientific research. Academic family in Belgrade with stable professional incomes. Lived in great-grandfather's apartment in Dorćol — established Belgrade family with educational capital.
ecosystem_summary: BKTV opportunity selected from 6,000+ applicants. RTS (national broadcaster) offer from general-director Aleksandar Tijanić who noticed her talents. Belgrade media ecosystem provided opportunities but not uniquely elite or frontier.

endowment_summary: Discovered table tennis in 3rd grade (~age 9) when teacher recommended she try the sport. World Championship singles runner-up at 19. Prodigy-level achievement in reaching world-level by 19, described as the only Korean player who could challenge Chinese players.
inherited_summary: Father was a merchant (상업), mother was a homemaker. Six children in the family, Yang was the youngest. Rural Jeollabuk-do province during South Korea's developing era. Working-class family with no table tennis connections.
ecosystem_summary: School teacher introduction at age 9 provided domain entry. Korean national table tennis system with structured training. Competed at Samsung Sports Center with national team coaching. Korean national pipeline provided elite competition exposure.

endowment_summary: Mother started training her at age 4. National team at 13. World Cup champion at 18. World No. 1 at 19. Five-time World Cup champion. Prodigy-level achievement with trajectory-changing early selection into the world's most competitive table tennis system.
inherited_summary: Father Liu Shu was a factory director (grinding wheel factory) in Fushun. Mother Wang Lifeng was a provincial table tennis player who became her first coach. Family separated — mother moved with Liu to another city at age 6, father stayed behind. Family soundproofed walls for practice. Middle-class with direct domain inheritance through mother.
ecosystem_summary: Chinese national table tennis system — the ultimate frontier geography as the epicenter of the sport. Coach Zhang Jingqing (who also coached grand slam winner Wang Nan) discovered her. Moved to Guangzhou at 7 for better training at Weilun Sports School. National team at 13 with world-class coaching infrastructure.

endowment_summary: Started handball at 13 after being rejected by hometown club Borac Banja Luka as 'untalented.' Used rejection as motivation. Reached World Championship bronze at 24 and Champions League at 26. Above-average ability but not identified as a prodigy; success driven by adversity and determination.
inherited_summary: Born in Banja Luka, Bosnia-Herzegovina. Displaced by Yugoslav wars, forced to leave home and move to Serbia. No family wealth or handball connections mentioned. War displacement created active disadvantage and instability.
ecosystem_summary: Partizan Belgrade provided development opportunity after displacement. Spanish Liga ASOBAL (Ademar León, Barcelona) and French league (Montpellier) provided elite club environments. Balkan handball tradition gave cultural context. Overcame adversity of war and rejection.

endowment_summary: World Championship gold at 25 and Olympic gold at 26 — Georgia's first judo world champion. Described as the hardest worker in his team, highly competitive. Elite athlete but achievements came at 25-26, not showing prodigy-level early indicators.
inherited_summary: Born in Kutaisi, Georgia, during the Soviet transition period. Little publicly documented about family background. Grew up during Georgia's economic and social upheaval following independence in 1991. No evidence of family wealth or domain connections.
ecosystem_summary: Kutaisi judo tradition — hometown of Olympic champion Davit Khakhailishvili who inspired every child. Coach Omar Merabishvili (who also coached Khakhailishvili) provided elite mentorship. Georgian national wrestling style provided base for judo. Strong national judo program.

endowment_summary: First sporting love was tennis, idolizing Pete Sampras. Turned to cricket at 17 — late for a professional cricketer. Identified by Dennis Lillee as a 'once-in-nine-lives' prospect. Natural athletic talent but late domain entry and no early cricket prodigy indicators.
inherited_summary: Born in Townsville, Queensland — 'little money and a disjointed home life, moving between relatives, never settled.' Working-class background in a rugby league stronghold, not a traditional cricket pathway. Financial and family instability created active disadvantage.
ecosystem_summary: Dennis Lillee's identification at 17 at a fast bowling clinic provided world-class mentor recognition. Australian Cricket Academy under Rod Marsh provided elite development pipeline. Queensland and Australian national team system. Back injuries and temporary quit in 2003 served as adversity catalysts.

endowment_summary: Started gymnastics at Shichahai Sports School at age 7-8. World Championship gold on uneven bars at 15 — first Chinese gymnast (male or female) to win a world title. Olympic gold at 20. Created eponymous uneven bars skills. Prodigy-level achievement with trajectory-changing early world title.
inherited_summary: Born in Beijing. No family information publicly available about parents' professions or wealth. Entered the state sports system at a young age, which provided comprehensive support but no evidence of family domain inheritance or wealth.
ecosystem_summary: Shichahai Sports School for Amateurs — China's premier gymnastics academy. Chinese national sports system provided comprehensive state support from a young age. Joined national team at 15. The Chinese state sports system is a once-in-a-generation pipeline for gymnastics, providing elite coaching, training, and competition access.

endowment_summary: Provincial team at 9, national team at 13. World Junior Championship Grand Slam at 17. World No. 1 at 24. Double Olympic gold medalist. Prodigy-level talent identified and cultivated from age 4.5, with trajectory-changing early selection into the world's most competitive system.
inherited_summary: Mother Pang Min was a table tennis player who won Shandong provincial 'Hope Cup' runner-up at 12 and multiple Qingdao city championships. Mother's coach Wu Naichan trained Chen Meng from age 4.5. Father Chen Liang supportive. Cousin is celebrity actor Huang Xiaoming. Direct domain inheritance through mother.
ecosystem_summary: Chinese national table tennis system — the ultimate frontier geography. Shandong provincial team at 9, national team at 13. Coached by mother's former coach Wu Naichan, then by Dong Xi at Qingdao. Chinese table tennis provides once-in-a-generation peer environment and coaching infrastructure.

endowment_summary: Started badminton at 8 to lose weight. National team at 15. Olympic gold in mixed doubles at 19 — youngest Olympic badminton champion from South Korea. Three gold medals at 2006 World Junior Championships. Exceptional early achievement in badminton.
inherited_summary: Mother signed him up for badminton club to lose weight. Rural Hwasun County in South Jeolla Province. No family badminton connections or wealth. Working-class rural background with no domain inheritance.
ecosystem_summary: South Korean national badminton pipeline — entered national team at 15. Coach Kang Kyung-jin. Partnerships with world-class players (Jung Jae-sung, Lee Hyo-jung, Yoo Yeon-seong). Hwasun County later built a stadium and memorial hall in his name, showing local investment in badminton.

endowment_summary: Started playing badminton at 6 under father's influence. Junior international debut at 16. World Championship at 23, Olympic gold at 24. Exceptional early achievement with long-term partnership with Markis Kido from age 14.
inherited_summary: Father Ferry Yoegianto was a badminton coach at Sinar Mutiara club in Pemalang. Two older sisters (Silvia, Ivon) also played badminton. Father drove him to training on motorcycle. Direct domain inheritance through father's coaching and family immersion in badminton.
ecosystem_summary: PB Jaya Raya (elite Indonesian badminton club) from age 13 — lived in dormitory. Pelatnas Cipayung (national training center). Partnership with Markis Kido from 1998. Indonesian national badminton system — one of the world's strongest. Coached by Christian Hadinata and other legends.

endowment_summary: Started badminton in elementary school when PE teacher picked her. National team in second year of high school. World Championship bronze at 20, Olympic exhibition gold at 22. Good athlete with early international achievement but not prodigy-level.
inherited_summary: Born in Jeungpyeong-gun, Chungcheongbuk-do — rural area. No family badminton connections mentioned. Attended local schools and Korea National Sport University. No evidence of family wealth or domain inheritance.

ecosystem_summary: Cuban sports school system provided training and competition pipeline from age 11. National team at 17. endowment_summary: Started table tennis at 7. National team at 13 — exceptionally early selection. World Cup at 20, World No. 1 at 20. Grand Slam champion (Olympic, World, World Cup). Prodigy-level achievement with trajectory-changing early selection into the world's most competitive system.

Spanish, German, and Macedonian top clubs. Overcame finger amputation injury (lost part of finger in 2008).

ecosystem_summary: HRK Izvidac (local club in Ljubuski) provided early senior opportunity at 15. CB Ademar Leon (top Spanish club) at 20. Croatian national team pipeline. Bosnian/Croatian handball tradition. Spanish Liga ASOBAL provided elite competition environment.

endowment_summary: Started handball at 5 following older sister Christina. National team debut at 25 — relatively late international arrival. European Championship gold in first major tournament. Good athlete but not prodigy-level; success came through persistence in elite club system.

Skjeberg HK provided transition. Norwegian national team system with elite coaching and competition.

endowment_summary: Described as 'surdoué du ballon' (prodigy with balls) — natural athletic ability across multiple ball sports. Started handball after stopping football. French champion at 20 with Montpellier. Good natural athlete but late to handball.

Selected for All Blacks at 20 after only 17 first-class games. NZ Under-21 and 'Baby Blacks' world championship in 1999. Once-in-a-generation rugby ecosystem.

endowment_summary: Started snooker at 9. First competitive century break at 12. Youngest European Under-19 champion at 14. Turned professional at 16. Youngest player to compete at the Crucible at 17. Prodigy-level achievement with trajectory-changing early dominance.

Family made significant financial and lifestyle sacrifices for his snooker career.

Belgian snooker ecosystem, though not a traditional powerhouse. Practice up to 15 hours a day on weekends. World Series of Snooker exposure at 14 beating professional champions.

Good athlete with strong arm but not identified as prodigy early; success came through development and conversion.

ecosystem_summary: Houston Astros academy in Venezuela — professional development pipeline. Scout Andres Reiner discovered him at 15 and personally drove 12 hours to recruit him. Academy converted him to pitcher. Minnesota Twins development system. Venezuelan baseball tradition provided cultural context.

endowment_summary: Started handball at 5 following babysitter who was a coach. National team debut at 19. Good student and competitive from young age. Solid athlete but not prodigy-level; success came through Danish system development.

inherited_summary: Son of Esther and Jack Mann, a grocer in Chicago. Jewish family; grandfather emigrated from Russian Empire. Working-class background — Mann worked as construction worker, short-order cook, and grocery clerk. No film industry connections or family wealth.
ecosystem_summary: London Film School (MA, 1967) — legitimate institution. 1960s London commercial film scene was a vibrant ecosystem. Contemporaries: Ridley Scott, Alan Parker, Adrian Lyne. Paris May 1968 student revolt access for NBC documentary. Worked at 20th Century Fox's British office. Right place, right time for emerging film scene.
